governing: shear rupture of the angles' net section (AISC 360-22 J4.2b): demand 142.863 kip, capacity 146.81 kip
notes: Petra PASS (check 2, identical to final.petra). Design: 2L4x3x3/8 A36, 3 in legs outstanding on the W14x61 web, 11.5 in long; 4 rows of 7/8 in A325-N (Group 120, threads included, snug-tight, standard holes) at 3 in pitch, Lev 1-1/4 in, top bolt 3 in below the beam top; beam gauge 2-1/4 in, setback 1/2 in, beam end distance 1-3/4 in; support gauge 3-7/8 in (1.74 in per leg). I hand-checked the main strengths and they match Petra. Next highest: outstanding-leg block shear 0.957, beam-side bolt group 0.941 (tearout of the bottom bolt in the angles plus bearing on the 0.395 in beam web), shear yield 0.767. The governing detailing check is edge distance at 0.90. Deformation at the bolt holes is taken as a design consideration (J3.11a). Petra does not check these: angle flexibility (3/8 in angles are within normal practice), the column itself, and whether the field bolts in the outstanding legs can be tightened past the shop bolts in the same rows. The outstanding legs have 1.74 in gauge, which leaves 1.37 in from each bolt to the beam-side leg against 1.33 in needed. The joint is snug-tight, so place the nuts on the far side of the column web or snug with a spud wrench, and confirm with the erector. Nothing frames into the other side of the column web. If a beam is added there, the shared bolts must be redesigned. The load is the user's factored shear, 0 to 142.863 kip, LRFD, with no axial force.
